# Bounded transport-close retry in git_push_to_dev

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC7). Implements the retry half of the
flake fix; the retry-policy tests come from the preceding test slice.

## Design (agreed direction — Q3 default)

- 3 attempts total (initial + 2 retries), jittered exponential backoff
  (~2 s, ~8 s, capped), retrying **only** the allowlisted transport patterns:
  `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`,
  `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`.
- Auth, branch-policy and every other error keeps today's behaviour;
  non-fast-forward keeps its existing dedicated rebase-and-retry recovery;
  `PushTimeoutError` is never retried (a timeout means the gate was running —
  replaying it multiplies cost).
- Every attempt uses the same cwd, argv and environment: the retry runs the
  pre-push hook again, which serves its cached full-suite entry. No bypass
  flag is ever injected.
- The attempt trail (count, backoff used, final reason) is logged and returned
  to the caller for reporting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Transient transport closes are retried with bounded backoff: `git_push_to_dev()` retries a transport-level close (`Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`) up to a bounded number of attempts with jittered exponential backoff, from the **same cwd** as the first attempt.
- [ ] It fails fast (no retry) on auth, branch-policy and non-fast-forward errors, and never retries a push timeout.
- [ ] The retry does not bypass the gate: the pre-push hook runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry, and the attempt count, backoff and reason are logged and reported.
- [ ] The push cwd stays whatever the caller resolved — the retry reuses it and hard-codes nothing, so the push-from-worktree change can land without rework.
- [ ] The transport-retry tests from the preceding test slice pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a transport-close allowlist predicate and retry constants (attempts,
   backoff base, cap) with injectable overrides for tests.
2. Wrap the existing spawn/communicate logic in a bounded attempt loop,
   preserving process-group kill on timeout and the non-fast-forward detection.
3. Log each attempt (`attempt i/N`, reason, backoff) and carry the trail on the
   raised/reported failure.
4. No change to call sites' signatures (`-> bool` stays; richer failures are
   raised).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` transport allowlist, attempt loop and backoff
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — retry-policy tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py` — finish interplay to keep green

- Only the recognised transport patterns retry — everything else fails as today (a retry must never mask a real error).

# Intake Brief — implement.py start cannot resume from inside a linked worktree (relative worktree path) (SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF)

> **Headline:** `implement.py start` computes its default worktree path relative to the repository root but resolves it against the *current* directory, so the documented driven-child resume (`cd` into the item's own worktree, then `start`) resolves a doubly-nested path, misses the registered worktree and fails in `git worktree add`. The fix — resolve the default path against the main checkout root — belongs to this repository.

## Migration note (moved from AI_Hell)

This defect was originally filed in the AI_Hell worklog as **AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY** (as a cross-repo discovery report), with the fix tracked here as a stub. The producer determined the item belongs entirely in this repository — `implement.py` lives here (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement`) and AI_Hell contains no `implement.py` — so the full intake brief, the effort/risk estimate and the `intake_complete` stage were migrated into this item and the AI_Hell item was deleted.

Nothing was lost in the move: the deleted item had no children, no dependency edges and only three comments (the intake scope note, the effort/risk report and an auto-dispatch marker), all reproduced or superseded here.

## Problem statement

A driven child session is expected to resume the worktree its parent already created: `cd` into `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and run `implement.py start <id>`. That resume path is broken. Because the default worktree path is repository-root-relative (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) and is resolved with `Path(wt_path).resolve()` while `cwd` is the worktree itself, the computed path becomes `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`; `_is_worktree()` therefore returns `False`, `git worktree add` is attempted at the nested path and fails, and the work item is released to `open`.

**Measurable outcome:** with the fix, the same command from the same `cwd` reports the existing absolute worktree path, emits no `Creating worktree at` line, creates no directory under `<worktree>/.worklog/`, and leaves the item `in_progress`.

## Users

- **Primary:** an agent session resuming a pre-created worktree (the `implement.py drive` / epic-child pattern, and any manual resume after a crash or context reset).
- **Secondary:** the producer/operator who relies on the documented "`start` resumes the pre-created worktree idempotently" contract and on `drive` completing each child in its own worktree.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of the agent framework, who must be able to trust that `start` and `finish` agree on the canonical worktree for an item.

User stories:

- *As a driven child agent,* I want `implement.py start <my-id>` run from inside my pre-created worktree to resume that worktree, so that the standard leaf workflow works unchanged and my work is not stranded.
- *As a producer,* I want resume to behave identically from the main checkout and from inside the worktree, so that a restarted or re-dispatched session cannot silently fail (or, worse, create a nested tree).

## Reproduction (verified 2026-10-31 during AH-0MVSE7F090010EG3)

1. A worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<ID>-<slug>` exists and is registered (`.git` is a file; `git worktree list` shows it) — e.g. created by `implement.py parent`/`drive`.
2. `cd .worklog/worktrees/wl-<ID>-<slug>`.
3. `python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py start <ID>`.
4. Observed: `INFO: Refreshing parent branch dev...` → `INFO: Creating worktree at .worklog/worktrees/wl-<ID>-<slug> from branch dev...` → `ERROR: Failed to create worktree at ...`; the item is released to `open`.

Workaround until fixed: pass the absolute path — `implement.py start <ID> --worktree-path <abs-worktree-path>`.

## Root cause (verified against current `dev`)

In `phase_start` → `_phase_start_locked()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:6761`):

```python
wt_path = worktree_path_override or worktree_path_for(work_item_id, slug)
branch = branch_name_for(work_item_id, slug)
abs_wt_path = str(Path(wt_path).resolve())
...
resumed = _is_worktree(Path(abs_wt_path))
```

- `worktree_path_for()` (`:539`) returns `f"{DEFAULT_WORKTREE_DIR}/wl-{work_item_id}-{slug}"`, i.e. **relative to the repository root** (`DEFAULT_WORKTREE_DIR = ".worklog/worktrees"`, `:209`).
- `Path(wt_path).resolve()` resolves that relative path against **`cwd`**.
- When `cwd` is the item's own worktree, `abs_wt_path` becomes `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`. `_is_worktree()` (`:10458`, true only when `.git` is a *file*) returns `False`.
- The code then calls `git_worktree_add(branch, wt_path, parent_branch)` (`:2337`) with the *relative* path, which git also resolves against `cwd` — a nested tree inside the worktree (or a hard failure).
- `_get_repo_root()` (`:3021`) already returns the **main checkout** even when invoked from inside a linked worktree (via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), and `phase_start` already computed `repo_root` a few lines earlier for the parent-branch refresh — the value is simply not used for the worktree path.

The sibling defect in the same flow (storing the worktree as `repo_root` in `.implement_state.json`) was fixed and regression-covered by `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py`; that test module documents that **mocking `_get_repo_root` is exactly why the defect escaped** earlier coverage.

## Desired change

1. Resolve the **default** worktree path against the main checkout root from `_get_repo_root()` (e.g. `Path(repo_root, worktree_path_for(...)).resolve()`), not `cwd`; preserve the current `Path.cwd()` fallback when `_get_repo_root()` returns `None`.
2. Keep `--worktree-path` authoritative, with unchanged semantics: an absolute override is used as given; a relative override continues to resolve against `cwd` (and that is documented).
3. Use the resolved **absolute** path consistently for the resume check, the `git worktree add` argument, the log lines, the start/resume comment, `.implement_state.json`, the signal globals and the `cd <path>` hint.
4. Regression test (see AC5) built on a real temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, with `_get_repo_root` **not** mocked.
5. Update the docs that state the resolution rule (see AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `implement.py start <id>` invoked with `cwd` inside the item's own registered worktree resumes that worktree: the report/comment says resumed, `git_worktree_add` is not called, and no nested `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` path is created.
- **AC2:** The default worktree path is resolved against the main checkout root from `_get_repo_root()` (never `cwd`); when `_get_repo_root()` returns `None` the previous `cwd` fallback is preserved.
- **AC3:** Running `start` from the main checkout still creates the worktree at `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no regression).
- **AC4:** `--worktree-path` remains authoritative with unchanged semantics (absolute used as given; relative resolved against `cwd`), and that semantics is documented.
- **AC5:** A regression test covers AC1 with a real temporary git repo plus a linked worktree and **no `_get_repo_root` mocking**, and fails against the pre-fix implementation.
- **AC6:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — at minimum the `_phase_start_locked()` comment/docstring, `worktree_path_for()` docstring, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (resume-from-worktree wording) and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (path-resolution rule).
- **AC7:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change the *canonical* worktree location (still `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`); only the base used to resolve a relative default path changes.
- `_get_repo_root()` may return `None` (not a git repo, git unavailable) — the pre-existing `cwd` fallback must remain so `start` degrades as before.
- Existing callers of `worktree_path_for()` keep receiving a repo-root-relative string (its contract is unchanged); the resolution change happens at the call site.
- Tests must use hermetic git fixtures (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env`) and must not touch the live checkout or the global skills install.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` is the canonical statement of the `repo_root` rule; any wording change there must not weaken the derived state-file `repo_root` contract.
- The change must keep the driven-child path working end-to-end (parent creates tree → child session resumes → child finishes), which is the scenario that regressed.

## Existing state

- The defect is present in `dev` at the time of intake (root cause verified in source, not merely reported).
- `_get_repo_root()` already implements the required main-checkout resolution and is covered by `test_repo_root_resolution.py`.
- The resume branch exists (`resumed = _is_worktree(abs_wt_path)`; `SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9`), so only the path base is wrong.
- Existing tests (`test_phase_start_claim.py`, `test_repo_root_resolution.py`, `test_phase_start_child_lock.py`) mock `_get_repo_root` or pass an absolute `--worktree-path`, which is why this case was not caught.
- Documented contract: `skill/implement/SKILL.md` states "`start` resumes the pre-created worktree idempotently"; `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` states the `repo_root` resolution rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()` worktree path computation/resume check (`:6761`), `worktree_path_for()` docstring (`:539`), reuse of `_get_repo_root()` (`:3021`); pass an absolute path to `git_worktree_add()` (`:2337`).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_worktree_resume.py` — new regression tests (real git fixtures; helper patterns from `test_repo_root_resolution.py`).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — resume-from-worktree wording (driven-child section).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — path-resolution rule under the `repo_root` section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — override semantics:** `--worktree-path` keeps its current meaning (absolute verbatim, relative against `cwd`). Changing relative-override resolution to the repo root would be a silent behaviour change for callers; it is deliberately not part of this fix (recorded in AC4).
- **Assumption — canonical location unchanged:** only the base for the *default* path changes, so no operator tooling or documentation that names the worktree directory needs updating beyond the resolution-rule wording.
- **Risk — symlink/path normalisation:** `Path.resolve()` also dereferences symlinks; resolving `repo_root` and the worktree path together must not change the reported path in the normal main-checkout case (regression risk for `report["worktree_path"]` and the state file). Covered by AC3/AC5.
- **Risk — drive orchestration:** `phase_drive`/`phase_sibling` invoke `start` via a subprocess (`_invoke_implement`) whose `cwd` varies; a fix that only special-cases "inside the worktree" rather than using `_get_repo_root()` would leave other `cwd` values broken. The chosen approach (always resolve against `_get_repo_root()`) avoids a cwd-shape table.
- **Risk — test realism:** mocks hid the sibling defect; the regression test must build a real repo/worktree. If the fixture is expensive, reuse the existing fixture helpers rather than duplicating them.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the slug-drift gap (title change → second worktree) and the `--worktree-path` relative-override question are out of scope; both are recorded (SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC and AC4 respectively) rather than folded in.
- **Risk — unchanged concurrency window:** between the `_is_worktree()` resume check and `git worktree add`, another actor can still register or remove the tree — the per-item child lock and the parent-branch lock already bound this, and this fix neither widens nor narrows it (no new locking is in scope).
- **Failure mode if unfixed:** driven-child sessions keep failing at resume; agents work around with an absolute `--worktree-path`, masking the bug and leaving orchestration dependent on undocumented behaviour.

## Related work

- Duplicate/overlap check performed (`wl search` in both stores): no other item covers this defect.
- **SA-0MVMMHG9Z004F2ED** — `finish` refuses to remove a resumed worktree because `phase_start` stored the worktree as `repo_root` (sibling defect in the same flow; its fixed regression suite is `test_repo_root_resolution.py`).
- **MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4** / `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py` — the `repo_root` = main-checkout rule this fix reuses (module docstring: mocking `_get_repo_root` is why the sibling defect escaped).
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — introduced the idempotent-resume branch that this defect defeats.
- **SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC** — follow-up filed during this intake: `start` creates a second worktree when the work-item title (slug) changed (out of scope here).
- Precedent for cross-repo discovery reports (now consolidated): `AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81` → `SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5`, `AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB` → `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No producer questions were required: the report contains a reproduction, a root cause that was re-verified in source, and a workaround. Decisions taken as research instead:

- **Q (self-resolved): Is the bug still present, or already fixed?** — Answer (Map): present. Evidence: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:6761` still resolves the repo-root-relative default path against `cwd`; `_get_repo_root()` is available but unused there.
- **Q (self-resolved): Should a relative `--worktree-path` override also be repo-root-relative?** — Answer (Map): no, keep current `cwd` semantics (AC4) to avoid a silent behaviour change; documented as an assumption for the producer to overturn if preferred.
- **Q (self-resolved): What about a title change altering the slug?** — Answer (Map): separate defect, filed as SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC (out of scope).
- **Q (producer): Where should this item live?** — Answer (Map): entirely here. `implement.py` is in this repository and AI_Hell has no copy; the AI_Hell discovery-report item was migrated into this item and deleted.

## Out of scope

- Slug-drift (title change → second worktree): SA-0MVXUHAM3006BRNC.
- Changing `--worktree-path` relative-override resolution semantics (AC4).
- Any new locking around the resume check / `git worktree add` window.

**Parent:** SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM — Finish main-checkout guard: failure-path verification + cross-checkout attribution (covers parent AC2, AC3 implementation halves).

**Blocked by** the sibling test item "Regression tests: cross-checkout attribution and fail-closed repo_root" (test-first).

## Problem

Two attribution defects:

1. `_resolve_main_repo_root` trusts `state.repo_root` whenever it is not the worktree or inside it, so a state file pointing at a sibling checkout makes finish snapshot, fast-forward and push a foreign repository.
2. `_record_finish_own_churn` returns the raw `git diff --name-only before after` list from `repo_root`; nothing constrains those paths to the repo being finished or to churn actually observed in that checkout, and `_main_checkout_guard_violations` allow-lists any listed path with a non-deletion code.

## Scope

- **Fail-closed `repo_root`.** In `_resolve_main_repo_root`, derive `main = _get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (git common dir parent) and require `state.repo_root` to resolve to that same root. On mismatch: log a loud WARNING naming the rejected and derived roots and use the derived root — never the stated foreign value. Keep the existing stale-state rejection, and keep the current fallback (stated root, or cwd discovery) only when derivation is impossible (`_get_repo_root` returns `None`), with a warning. Never return a path outside the repo that owns the worktree.
- **Constrained `own_churn`.** In `_record_finish_own_churn`: resolve `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `--git-common-dir` for `repo_root` and refuse (return `[]` + warning) when they disagree with `repo_root`; drop every path that is absolute, contains `..`, or does not resolve inside `repo_root`; and intersect the diff list with the paths actually observed dirty in the finished checkout (pass the post-fast-forward snapshot in, or re-snapshot inside the helper). Report dropped/not-observed paths as a `not_observed` diagnostic in `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]` — visible, never allow-listed.
- Only record `own_churn` when the fast-forward actually advanced the checkout (`method == "advanced"`); a refused/no-op fast-forward contributes an empty list.
- Keep the invariant that a deletion (`D`) is never allow-listed, and keep SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG's benign-concurrent-churn exclusion intact (no new false positives for a clean run).
- Document the contract in the affected docstrings (`_resolve_main_repo_root`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`).

**Parent ACs restated verbatim below** (the plan's AC coverage review measures similarity against them); this item's own checks follow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Attribution correctness.** `own_churn` never lists paths belonging to another checkout/repo, and the guard's `repo_root` resolution can never resolve to, or act on, a path outside its own repo. A test asserts foreign paths are not allow-listed and are reported as violations instead.
- `_resolve_main_repo_root` returns the main checkout derived from the worktree whenever that is derivable, and never a stated `state.repo_root` that disagrees with it; the mismatch produces a WARNING naming both paths.
- With an underivable main root (non-git worktree), the documented fallback + warning behaviour is unchanged (existing harness and tests stay green).
- `_record_finish_own_churn` returns only paths inside the finished repo that were observed dirty in that checkout after the fast-forward; foreign, absolute, escaping and not-observed paths are dropped and surfaced as a diagnostic, never allow-listed.
- A refused or no-op fast-forward yields an empty `own_churn`.
- Deletions remain never-allow-listed, and a clean finish still passes with no false-positive abort (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG).
- All tests from the sibling test item pass on the fixed tree and fail on the pre-fix tree; changed-scope gate green via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_main_repo_root`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`, `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`, `phase_finish` Step 5/5b.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_repo_root_resolution.py`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — attribution/allow-list precedent.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — contract wording owned by the docs item.

- SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (completed) — attribution allow-list precedent; must not regress.
- SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN (blocked) — push from the worktree holding the commit: Step-5 fast-forward + pre-push guard interplay.

# ship: CHANGELOG release section is discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

**Origin:** observed in the `1916: The Rising` v0.1.23 release (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L). The Discord release notification went out with no release focus and no changelog body, and `main`'s `CHANGELOG.md` had no `## v0.1.23` section.

## Root cause

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` the CHANGELOG is generated **before** `origin/dev` is merged:

1. `generate-changelog.js "$NEW_VERSION"` writes `## v0.1.23 (…)` (with the `> **Release focus:** …` marker) and commits it on the release branch, which is based on `main`.
2. `git merge --no-ff origin/dev` then conflicts on `CHANGELOG.md`, because `dev` carries its own `## Unreleased` block.
3. The auto-resolution runs `git checkout --theirs CHANGELOG.md` — taking dev's whole file and **discarding the generated release section**.
4. The merged tree is tagged, so the released tree carries no `## v<version>` section.

The comment above the resolution (lines 217-219) even claims "generate-changelog.js rewrites it for the new version **afterwards**", contradicting the actual order.

Downstream effects:
- `discord-notify.js` `extractChangelogSection()` returns `null` and `extractReleaseFocus()` finds no marker, so the embed loses both the focus and the release notes (silently — only a focus warning is logged).
- Release notes are absent from `main`/`dev` for that version (recoverable only from the discarded commit).

## Proposed fix

1. Preserve the generated section across the merge: when `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts, take dev's version and then **re-insert** the generated `## v<version>` section (a small, tested helper), instead of discarding it.
2. Assert after the merge that a generated section is still present; abort the release (before tagging) if it was lost. A *failed generation* keeps today's non-fatal behaviour (warn and continue) — this only guards the regression where a successfully generated section is dropped.
3. `discord-notify.js`: log an explicit warning naming the version when no `## v<version>` section is found (still non-blocking).
4. Document the guarantee in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/changelog-merge.js` (new helper)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_changelog_merge.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance criteria

1. With dev's `CHANGELOG.md` modified (an `## Unreleased` block present), the merge-resolution path yields a file that contains the generated `## v<version>` section with its `> **Release focus:**` marker **and** keeps dev's content — asserted by a node test over the new merge helper using a dev-style file.
2. When a section was generated but is missing after the merge, the release script aborts before tagging with an actionable message (non-zero exit) — asserted by a test of the resolution helper's "section lost" outcome plus the script-level guard.
3. A failed generation keeps the non-fatal contract: the release continues with an explicit warning, and the guard does not fire for a section that was never generated — asserted by a test.
4. `discord-notify.js` emits an explicit warning naming the version when the `## v<version>` section is absent, and still sends the notification (non-blocking) — unit test with an injected fetch.
5. The Discord embed still carries both the release focus and the changelog body when a generated section is present — unit test on the composition path.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the ordering/preservation guarantee and the abort-on-loss behaviour.

## Goal (user story)

*As an agent finishing a work item*, I need a slot waiter to take **any** free
slot in its namespace no matter how long it has been waiting, so a green change
is never blocked for hours while capacity sits idle (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) probes
only `range(self.max_workers)`, and `max_workers` is resolved once in
`__init__`. A waiter that started when the pool held two slots therefore never
sees slots `2..7` created later by higher-ceiling processes — the observed
105-minute stall. The poll cadence is already bounded (50 ms base, jittered
`[0.5, 1.5]x`); there is **no** unbounded backoff in the shipped code. The
defect is the fixed-index probe.

This is the implementation slice; it turns the strict-`xfail` regressions from
the two test children green by removing their markers.

## Scope

`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`:

1. **Dynamic discovery.** Replace the `range(self.max_workers)` probe with a
   namespace scan: each attempt enumerates the numeric slot files currently
   present in the slot directory (deterministic ascending index order) and
   `flock`s the first free one. Slots created by a later, higher-ceiling
   process are therefore usable.
2. **Effective-ceiling rule.** The effective pool is the **union of slot files
   present** in the namespace; the caller's own `max_workers` is a *floor it
   guarantees* (it still creates `0..max_workers-1`), never a host-wide limit it
   may exceed. `_ensure_slots()` stays bounded by `max_workers`.
3. **Fail-fast stays fail-fast.** `timeout=0` performs one scan plus one
   `flock` attempt — no sleep, no blocking work added by the scan
   (`audit_runner` enters with `timeout=0`).
4. **Bounded cadence documented.** Keep the existing 50 ms base and jittered
   `[0.5, 1.5]x` retry; document the maximum poll interval (75 ms jittered, 50 ms
   unjittered) and that no backoff may grow without a documented cap. Record the
   measured directory-scan cost (a single `scandir()` of a directory with ~10
   entries) in the docstring or a comment.
5. **Docstring contract.** The module docstring documents the discovery rule,
   the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval.
6. **Preserve** the kernel-`flock` model (no PID bookkeeping, no stale locks, no
   daemon), jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation
   (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`).

## Constraints

- **Do not change the configured ceiling.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` /
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics stay as shipped (`SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z`).
- **Do not implement ordering/fairness.** The FIFO turnstile is owned by
  `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`; the discovery scan must remain compatible with a future
  ticket layer (do not restructure acquisition into a queue).
- **Do not touch the `slot_busy` notice** — it keeps meaning genuine saturation.
- **Remove the strict `xfail` markers** added by the two test children as part of
  this slice.
- UK English; no ad-hoc suite invocations (`/skill:test`).

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — discovery scan, effective-ceiling and poll-interval docstring contract.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — strict `xfail` markers removed; regressions green.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process regression green.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — saturation notice regression must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A waiter whose ceiling is 2 acquires a free slot with index `>= 2` that already exists in the namespace, within one poll interval plus one `flock` attempt.
- **AC2** A waiter still creates at most its own `max_workers` slot files (`0..max_workers-1`); it never creates higher-index slots.
- **AC3** `timeout=0` remains fail-fast: exactly one scan plus one attempt, no sleep, no added blocking work (asserted by test).
- **AC4** The strict `xfail` markers from both test children are removed and all their assertions pass.
- **AC5** Jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`) behaviour is unchanged — their existing tests still pass.
- **AC6** The module docstring documents the discovery rule, the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval (including the measured directory-scan cost); no backoff without a documented cap.
- **AC7** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics and the `slot_busy` notice are untouched; build plus changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC8** The full project test suite passes for the change (enforced by the dev-push gate; any gate-reported failure is triaged per the test-failure policy, not worked around).

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC1** — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free: a waiter that began polling when only slots 0..N-1 existed must acquire within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one flock attempt) as soon as any slot file in its namespace is free, including slot files created by a later, higher-ceiling process; a max_workers=2 waiter acquires one of the new slots created after it began polling, well inside its timeout.
- **Parent AC2** — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff: the poll cadence has a documented maximum interval (50 ms base, jittered 0.5-1.5x when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll cycles, not one); no backoff may grow without a documented cap.

## Goal

Make Phase 1, Phase 2 deep analysis and the verdict re-ask survive transient Local Proxy
connection failures (bounded, slot-aware retry) and, when they truly cannot, fail with an
actionable message that names the cause instead of a generic "Connection error." verdict.

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-context audit to either complete or
tell me exactly why it could not (phase, attempt count, elapsed, provider/pool cause), so a
transient proxy hiccup cannot permanently block a release with no diagnosis.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- The failing prompts measured 5.7–6.7 KB — smaller than a succeeding 6.3 KB sibling — and the
  exact captured prompt replays with HTTP 200 today. The "oversized request / truncate the
  payload" hypothesis is **not** supported.
- Retries failed in 11–387 ms (`stopReason: error`, "Connection error."), i.e. fast connection
  failures inside Pi's 2 s/4 s/8 s auto-retry budget, while the Local Proxy (3-slot pool) was
  serving another project's audit. `_PHASE2_MAX_RETRIES = 1` and the Phase-1 budget give no
  slot-aware backoff, and the verdict re-ask has no retry of its own.
- The provider-error path marks every AC `partial` with "Pi provider error: Connection error."
  and sets `ctx.script_failure`, which then triggers the Defect 2 persistence path.

## Scope

- Add a bounded, slot-aware recovery policy for provider *connection* errors in
  `phase2_deep`, `phase2_child`, `phase2_batch`, the Phase-1 parent/child screens and
  `verdict_reask`: a small number of retries with increasing backoff that yield the concurrency
  slot (so parallel audits do not retry-storm a saturated pool), capped so a single item cannot
  hang a release.
- Distinguish "proxy/pool unavailable" from a content/parse failure, and surface it in the
  report evidence with the phase, attempt count, elapsed seconds and the underlying error text.

  timestamp, appended to the stable key set) so an operator can always tell whether the numbers
  they are reading came from the attempt they just ran — and so a stale stored report cannot be
  mistaken for the current attempt.

## Implementation notes (Option B+)

**Rule implemented** (single decision point per run):
- Pass top-level: preserve the stored `false` (write no flag) when a prior **passing** stored audit's v2 content fingerprint equals the pre-audit content fingerprint and `needsProducerReview == false`; otherwise write `--needs-producer-review yes`.
- Fail top-level, independent: write `--needs-producer-review yes` regardless of `merge_gate_blocker`.
- Kids, cascade-demotion-suppressed `No`, infra-failure/unparseable/tainted `No`: flag untouched (no set, no clear).
- The runner only ever writes `yes` or nothing — it never writes `no`.

**Where:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: `prior_audit` + `producer_review` on `_AuditContext`; `_summarise_prior_audit` / `_fetch_prior_audit` / `_producer_review_preserved` / `_resolve_producer_review_decision` / `_format_producer_review_line` / `_append_producer_review_metadata`; `_compute_fallback_tainted` extracted so the lifecycle and the decision share one taint rule.
- Pre-audit capture: non-forced path reuses the freshness gate's own `wl audit-show` via the new `audit_sink` out-param (zero added `wl` calls); forced path adds exactly one `wl audit-show` (the `--force`/ship-`--refresh-audits` recurrence path).
- Decision is resolved once before persistence and reused by `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`, so the persisted report and the flag write cannot disagree.
- Persisted report carries a `Producer review: preserved|required|untouched (<reason>)` metadata line (AC4). The metadata line is appended to the report text the runner hands to `persist_audit` (no `persist_audit` signature change needed); dry runs store no report and write no line.
- Merge-gate fail-closed report also carries the line.

**Tests** (default suite): new `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_producer_review.py` (predicate truth table, resolver branches, AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC6 transitions, cascade-suppressed `No`, audit-show-unavailable fail-safe, merge-gate parity, report metadata). `wl_helpers.audit_show_response` added as the pre-audit audit-record knob.
